specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: The top-level ROLLBACK of a failed transaction fails on the client; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). Then arm the client-side fault: the next top-level ROLLBACK fails in the driver and is not sent.
Raise an application error inside the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK, which fails, so the connection keeps its open transaction.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: Programmatic TransactionTemplate. HikariCP 7.1.0 with maximumPoolSize 1. No other pool setting is changed. Between the two units the connection is released through Spring's normal path. The pool is not closed, the connection is not evicted, and no validation query is issued between them. TX-03 runs only in this mode and in declarative-pooled.

configuration.rollbackRule: TransactionTemplate default: RuntimeException and Error. A checked SQLException is rethrown as SqlUnchecked where the case needs it to leave the callback.

execution.form: Programmatic: TransactionTemplate on DataSourceTransactionManager. PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. Writes are PreparedStatement calls on the connection DataSourceUtils.getConnection returns.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): the top-level ROLLBACK fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: Unit 1's transaction stays open on its connection ("idle in transaction"), holding the doomed write.
fault.expected_client: An error from the framework's rollback; what the framework then does with the connection is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its ROLLBACK failed, so it knows that the connection's transaction state is unknown.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute threw a throwable the callback did not throw
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) obtains a transaction, runs the callback, and calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns. On a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. On any other throwable it rolls back and throws java.lang.reflect.UndeclaredThrowableException. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, rollbackOnException stores the callback throwable with initApplicationException and throws the TransactionSystemException instead. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCommit calls Connection.commit and translateException wraps a SQLException as TransactionSystemException("JDBC commit failed", ex). Connection.commit is void and does not return a command tag. A normal return from execute is reported as committed. The callback's own throwable leaving execute is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving execute is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." Its note says actual nested transactions work on DataSourceTransactionManager. DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." No custom rollback rule is installed on the template. TransactionCallback cannot throw a checked SQLException. Where a case needs that error to leave the callback, the callback rethrows it as SqlUnchecked, a RuntimeException, so the template's RuntimeException rule sees it. That wrap is application code. It is not JdbcTemplate's exception translation.

error.message: JDBC rollback failed: application error: unit 1 fails: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK was not sent

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "next" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit2-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the next unit of work was attempted
the withheld ROLLBACK left unit 1's transaction open: its session was in a transaction holding unit 1's ID
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 9491; transactionid locks [9491]
